title: Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights
gist: Pseudonymous researcher Nightmare Eclipse dropped SignDrop, an unpatched Windows zero-day in the Common Log File System that abuses Windows Defender to give local users System rights and could disable any antivirus/EDR; it stems from an October 2025 Microsoft CLFS mitigation, but Will Dormann found it only works on certain aged Windows 11 26H2 systems.

insights.claim: SignDrop is a Windows zero-day in the Common Log File System (CLFS) that lets a user with ordinary rights escalate to full System privileges by forcing a privileged process such as Windows Defender to open a crafted CLFS container.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Another unpatched local privilege escalation in Windows raises enterprise endpoint risk.
insights.locator: On Tuesday, Nightmare Eclipse disclosed SignDrop

insights.claim: The SignDrop exploit calls Defender's legitimate ServerMpUpdateEngineSignature function and manipulates Object Manager symbolic links so CLFS creates a missing authentication file with Defender's System privileges while assigning it the original file's access control list.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Shows how chaining legitimate OS components creates exploitable logic flaws that are hard to patch.
insights.locator: By manipulating Windows Object Manager symbolic links

insights.claim: The SignDrop vulnerability stems from a security mitigation Microsoft introduced in October 2025 to stop attackers exploiting other CLFS vulnerabilities.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Security hardening can itself introduce new attack surface, complicating patch-quality assumptions.
insights.quote: Ironically, the vulnerability stems from a security measure Microsoft introduced in October 2025

insights.claim: Nightmare Eclipse claims SignDrop can be used against any antimalware engine to bypass tamper protection, since file creation appears to come from the security product's own legitimate process, making it able to turn off any antivirus/EDR.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: A generic EDR-disable technique would threaten the value proposition of endpoint security vendors until mitigated.
insights.quote: this makes this vulnerability unique as it can be used to turn off any antivirus/EDR
insights.locator: What makes it funnier is the fact

insights.claim: Nightmare Eclipse says SignDrop works on Windows 11 26H2, Windows 11 26H2 Experimental and Windows Server 2025 Experimental, and systems whose CLFS authentication mode is in learning or enforcement mode are vulnerable.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Exposure is concentrated in newest Windows builds, limiting near-term blast radius.
insights.locator: Nightmare Eclipse said the exploit worked

insights.claim: Researcher Will Dormann reproduced SignDrop but found it appears to require a Windows 11 26H2 system that has existed for more than 90 days, and only one of his many machines met the requirement.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Practical exploitability is narrower than the headline suggests.
insights.quote: you can’t just take a new 26H2 system and install updates and have it work
insights.locator: Researcher Will Dormann said in an interview

insights.claim: Because Microsoft does staged rollouts of Windows updates like 26H2, it is unclear how many systems are exposed to SignDrop, and Microsoft did not respond to a request for comment.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Uncertain exposure plus no vendor response leaves enterprises to self-assess.
insights.locator: Microsoft does staged rollouts of Windows updates

insights.claim: Nightmare Eclipse, a pseudonymous researcher with an ongoing public feud with Microsoft, has published numerous Windows zero-days in recent months without coordinated disclosure.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: A steady stream of unpatched public Windows exploits is a recurring reputational and operational risk for Microsoft.
insights.quote: Nightmare Eclipse, the pseudonym of a researcher with an ongoing, very public beef with Microsoft
insights.locator: Nightmare Eclipse, the pseudonym of a researcher
